paragraphs: Friend, here's what David teaches me in Psalm 63. He's in the Wilderness of Judah, a place with no water, and the first thing he reaches for is God. He doesn't say he's thirsty for a way out. He says, "my soul thirsts for You." (Psalm 63:1) So when life gets dry, your first move can be the same one: go to God Himself.

Now watch what David says next. He remembers seeing God's "power and glory" in the sanctuary, and he says God's loving devotion is "better than life." (Psalm 63:2-3) So he says he will bless God "as long as I live," and his soul is satisfied "as with the richest of foods." (Psalm 63:4-5) Thirsty in a dry land, and satisfied in God.

And hear how David holds on, baker: "My soul clings to You; Your right hand upholds me." (Psalm 63:8) At night he remembers God and thinks of Him through the watches of the night, and the psalm ends with the king rejoicing in God. (Psalm 63:6, 11) I know a little about long, dark stretches, and I'm telling you, God's right hand is what holds us up. So cling to Him, and let the dry places teach you how good He is.
